gaps.explanation: Statement pp5-6 Total Governmental Funds Total revenues 18,229,034 = General 8,790,960 + Economic Development 1,656,099 + Special Projects 400,823 + Debt Service 325,318 (p5) + Streets 4,131,202 + Capital Projects 1,181,408 + Other Governmental Funds 1,743,224 (p6). detail[] 12,956,164 = budget-basis schedules General p13 8,647,294 + Economic Development p14 2,227,711 + Special Projects p15 337,935 + nonmajor combining pp16-17 1,743,224 (= Other Governmental Funds column). (1) Missing fund columns (no schedule, nothing in detail[]): Debt Service Fund (p5) Property taxes 1,068 + Special assessments 37,422 + Interest 286,828 = 325,318; Streets Fund (p6) Property taxes 514,245 + Sales taxes 557,368 + Miscellaneous taxes 2,328,991 + Intergovernmental 389,695 + Charges for services 1,823 + Interest 338,244 + Miscellaneous 836 = 4,131,202; Capital Projects Fund (p6) Property taxes 965,452 + Miscellaneous taxes 146,136 + Interest 69,820 = 1,181,408; total 5,637,928 (added). (2) Different basis (no fix): General budget p13 8,647,294 vs GAAP p5 8,790,960 = -143,666; Economic Development p14 2,227,711 vs p5 1,656,099 = +571,612; Special Projects p15 337,935 vs p5 400,823 = -62,888; net +365,058. Check: 12,956,164 + 5,637,928 - 365,058 = 18,229,034. After the fix the schedule is 365,058 above the statement, the budget-basis vs GAAP difference of these three funds. The Streets Fund's printed other financing sources (Proceeds from sale of capital asset 16,043, Bonds issued 3,990,000, Bond discount (30,220), p6) are added with the column as other financing lines; they are not revenue and not transfers.
